chunks: And they remember only as God wills: He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness.

key_terms.التَّقْوَىٰ: Piety or God-consciousness; the quality of being worthy of reverence
key_terms.الْمَغْفِرَةِ: Forgiveness; the act of covering or pardoning sins
key_terms.يَشَاءَ: He wills; divine volition or decree

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God is worthy of Taqwa and Maghfirah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the interplay between divine will and human agency, affirming that while God is the ultimate source of piety and forgiveness, human beings are accountable for their remembrance of Him. It serves as a theological anchor in Surah Al-Muzzammil, linking the command to stand in night prayer with the assurance that sincere devotion leads to divine mercy. The phrase 'He is the Lord of Taqwa' highlights that true reverence is not merely ritualistic but rooted in God's attribute of granting forgiveness to those who strive for closeness.
